name: James Uthmeier

items.text: The Hope Florida Foundation gave $10 million to two nonprofit groups. They gave the money to a political committee headed by Uthmeier. A grand jury report called the money "misappropriated" but indicted no one. On Oct. 7, 2026, an appeals court ordered the report expunged. No charges have been filed.
items.why: This is a serious self-dealing-type accusation under criterion 6 that no court or prosecutor has decided: no charges, the grand jury report expunged, and a rehearing request pending.

items.text: On June 17, 2025, a federal judge held Uthmeier in civil contempt over an April 23 letter to police. The letter said he couldn't stop arrests under a blocked immigration law. She ordered biweekly reports, with no fine or jail. He wrote: "If being held in contempt is what it costs... so be it."
items.why: A federal court's contempt finding for defying its order is a misuse of the office under criterion 6; it fits no weight level exactly, so it takes the nearest, minor, because the sanction was reporting only and the appeal is unresolved.
check: If being held in contempt is what it costs... so be it.

items.text: Challenger José Javier Rodríguez, campaigning on "crime, costs and corruption," has criticized no-bid contracts and conditions at the Alligator Alcatraz detention site. No court finding on the contract claims was found, and Uthmeier's own role in awarding them has not been shown.
items.why: This is an opponent's allegation under criterion 6 with no finding and no shown conduct by Uthmeier in awarding contracts.
Nothing was documented on foreign ties (criterion 2), so there is no conduct to weigh.

for_review: 1) The WGCU, WLRN (Oct 8) and WLRN (Sept 30) pages came back mostly as site menus. I relied on their headers and descriptions, so the Hope Florida text is thin. Read the full opinion and Uthmeier's response. His office called the ruling a 'complete and total victory'; I saw that only in search snippets. Also check the pending rehearing motion and the reported IRS whistleblower claim, and the Tampa Bay Times and WUSF coverage. Item 1 could arguably be 'context' instead of 'open'. 2) Contempt: I found no 11th Circuit result on his appeal of the contempt order (ACLU and WFSU say he appealed). The 11th Circuit oral argument on SB 4-C was reportedly set for October 2026, so check the current status. Weight 1 is a judgment call. 3) Alligator Alcatraz: I could not read Rodríguez's specific claims. Snippets said the state emergency-management division operates the site, and a GAO report cited operation without a contract or agreement in place. Neither shows Uthmeier steering contracts. Wikipedia mentions vendor donations to him, and a donation proves nothing. 4) The owner-sites search found nothing about Uthmeier. 5) The foreign-ties check rests on the provided notes; I ran no FARA search of my own. 6) A search snippet said Uthmeier won the Nov 2026 election; this was not verified.
